name: ElectricSQL
tagline: Read-path sync engine that streams partial replicas of Postgres to clients over plain HTTP.
description: Electric is an open-source sync service that sits next to PostgreSQL, consumes logical replication and streams subsets of tables (shapes) to clients over HTTP, so CDNs can cache and fan out the data. Clients get a live, incrementally updated copy in memory, in TanStack DB or in PGlite. Writes go back through your own API, which keeps authorization and business logic in your backend. After the 2024 rewrite it is simpler and more scalable than the original CRDT-based ElectricSQL. In August 2026 the team joined Databricks (Neon) and began winding down Electric Cloud, while the Apache-2.0 sync engine stays open source.
statusNote: Team joined Databricks (Neon) in Aug 2026 and Electric Cloud is winding down; the Apache-2.0 sync engine remains open source and self-hostable.

pricing.notes: Self-hosting is free. Electric Cloud is being wound down after the Databricks deal.

scale.notes: Shape logs are served over HTTP and can be fanned out through CDNs; write throughput is bounded by the source Postgres.

strengths: Works with an existing Postgres; no schema rewrite or new primary database
Plain HTTP shape streams cache in CDNs and scale to many concurrent clients
Writes stay in your API, so auth and validation logic stay where they are
Pairs with PGlite and TanStack DB for a full local Postgres in the browser
weaknesses: Read-path only; optimistic writes and conflict handling are your job
Hosted Electric Cloud is winding down, so you must self-host
Future roadmap now depends on Databricks/Neon priorities
Shape filters are limited compared with arbitrary SQL
useCases: Local-first web apps with a Postgres backend
Streaming per-user data subsets to many clients
notIdealFor: Apps needing turnkey bidirectional offline writes
Teams that want a fully managed sync service
